transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can I start by asking your name and what brings you in today?

Hi, I'm Jessica. Um, I came in today because... well, I just barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. Like, I used to love dance class, hiking, trying new recipes... 

Actually, speaking of recipes, I used to make this amazing baked ziti. My neighbor Mrs. Gable gave me the recipe back when I lived in my old apartment—the one with the terrible plumbing where the kitchen sink would always back up? Anyway, she used a mix of ricotta and cottage cheese, which sounds weird, but it makes it so much fluffier. I tried to teach my sister how to make it last year, but she never pays attention to the oven timer and always burns the edges. She's just impatient, I guess. 

But, um... yeah. Trying new recipes, or even just regular game night with my friends... all of it just sits there now like chores I keep putting off. I just don't have it in me to do them anymore. I haven't even bought the cheese to make that ziti in months.
How long have you been feeling this way about things you used to enjoy?

Um, it's been a while. I think it all really started right after the robbery at this festival job I was working... that was about two years and three months ago. Which is a shame, because that job was actually really fun before that happened. We were selling these hand-carved wooden bowls and wind chimes, and the guy who made them, Arthur, he was this older guy with a huge white beard. He kind of looked like Santa Claus? He used to bring his golden retriever, Buster, to the booth every day. 

Buster was the absolute sweetest dog, he would just lay under the folding tables and sleep through all the loud music from the main stage. I always wanted a dog like that, you know? But my landlord doesn't allow pets over twenty pounds, which is such a stupid rule because small dogs bark way more than big dogs anyway. My neighbor's Chihuahua literally never shuts up, especially when the mail carrier comes, it just echoes in the hallway... but, um, what were we talking about? Oh, right. Yeah, so it's been about two years and three months since I really felt like doing much.
Have you noticed a change in your energy levels or do you feel more tired than usual lately?

Um, energy levels? I mean, I guess I'm not really sure. I don't think I'm more tired than usual, exactly. But speaking of being tired, my sister has been complaining constantly about how exhausted she is lately. She just started this new diet where she only eats things that are, like, raw? Or maybe it's just juicing, I don't even know. She bought this incredibly expensive blender, one of those Vitamix ones that sound like an airplane taking off in your kitchen. 

I told her she could just buy regular juice at the store, but she insists it has to be fresh-pressed. She made me try this green one last week that had kale and ginger and I swear, half a celery stalk just floating in it. It tasted like lawn clippings. And she wonders why she has no energy! I keep telling her she needs carbs, like that baked ziti I was talking about earlier, but she won't listen. She's always been stubborn like that, ever since we were kids. Like this one time when we were little, she refused to wear anything but her Halloween costume—this sparkly princess dress—for a whole month... wait, did that answer your question? I don't really think my energy is any different, no.
Jessica, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, more days than not?

Um, feeling down or depressed? I don't really think so. Not like, sad all day or anything. I mean, my mom is the one who gets really depressed. She actually has this special lamp she sits in front of during the winter because she says the gray weather makes her sad. It's supposed to mimic sunlight, I think? But it is so incredibly bright. I went over to her house last December to help her wrap Christmas presents—she always buys these huge, awkward things to wrap, like a globe for my nephew, how do you even wrap a sphere without it looking terrible? 

Anyway, I walked into her living room and it was like staring into the actual sun. I had spots in my vision for like ten minutes. I told her she's going to blind herself or give her cat cataracts. Her cat, Mr. Whiskers, he just sits right next to the lamp soaking it up like he's on a beach in Florida. He's a rescue, she found him under her porch during a thunderstorm... but yeah, no, I don't really feel sad or depressed most of the time. Just the whole not caring about things part.
Jessica, have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, make decisions, or think clearly lately?

Um, focus? Yeah, actually, that's been really hard lately. When I try to work on catering forms or, like, a Chamber application, I just end up reading the same line over and over again. And then I get totally stuck on these tiny choices, like what price to put down or which email I should answer first. It's so frustrating. 

Speaking of emails, my friend Sarah keeps forwarding me these massive chain emails about, like, conspiracy theories and weird home remedies? The other day she sent one about how putting onions in your socks cures the flu. Which is ridiculous, right? I mean, who wants to sleep with onions on their feet? Your sheets would smell like a deli for weeks. I buy these really nice lavender-scented laundry pods, they're kind of expensive, but they make everything smell like a spa. I tried telling Sarah to just buy regular medicine, but she’s totally convinced big pharma is hiding the cure in produce aisles. She even started growing her own garlic on her apartment balcony... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, my focus. Yeah, it's just really hard to think clearly and make decisions right now.
Jessica, have you noticed any changes in your weight recently, like losing or gaining a significant amount without trying?

Um, weight changes? No, I don't think so. My clothes all fit the same, so I haven't really noticed anything like that. But you know who has lost a ton of weight? My neighbor, Gary. He started doing that thing where you only eat for like eight hours a day and then starve for the rest of it. Intermittent fasting, I think it's called? He was telling me all about it when we were both taking our trash out on Tuesday. 

He lost like thirty pounds, but honestly, he looks kind of miserable. And he's always talking about food now. He asked me what I was making for dinner, and when I told him I was just doing a frozen pizza—because who has the energy to cook on a Tuesday, right?—he looked at me like I was eating gold. I get those rising crust ones from the supermarket, the pepperoni and sausage ones. Sometimes I add extra cheese on top because they never put enough on. You have to put it under the broiler for the last two minutes to get the cheese perfectly bubbly. I burned the roof of my mouth so badly last time I made one because I didn't wait for it to cool down. It peeled for like three days... wait, did I answer your question? Oh, yeah, no, my weight hasn't really changed at all.
Jessica, have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety more than before?

Um, moving slower or being fidgety? Not really, no. I don't feel like I'm moving through molasses or bouncing off the walls or anything. But speaking of moving slow, you should see the line at the post office lately. It is unbelievable. I went there yesterday to mail a birthday card to my aunt—she lives in Arizona, and she collects these little ceramic owls, so I always try to find a card with an owl on it. This year I found one that actually hoots when you open it. It's kind of obnoxious, but she loves that stuff. 

Anyway, there was only one person working the counter, this guy who looked like he was about a hundred years old, and he was typing with just his two index fingers. Just... peck... peck... peck. And the woman in front of me was trying to ship, like, six huge boxes to Germany, and she hadn't filled out any of the customs forms. She was arguing with the guy about whether she had to declare the homemade jam she was sending. Which, by the way, why would you ship glass jars of jam internationally? That just seems like a disaster waiting to happen. If one of those breaks, everything in the box is going to be sticky forever. I spilled maple syrup in my car trunk once like three years ago, and my spare tire is still stuck to the floorboard... but yeah, no, I haven't noticed any changes with my own moving or speaking. I feel pretty normal in that way.
Jessica, have you ever felt like life isn’t worth living or had thoughts about ending your life?

Um, thoughts about ending my life? No, definitely not. I've never felt like that. I mean, things are hard right now, but I wouldn't ever do that. You know who does talk about that stuff all the time, though? Those true crime podcasts. I started listening to this one last week, it's about this old hotel in Los Angeles where all these weird things happened. 

The host has this really soothing voice, kind of like an NPR announcer, but he's talking about the most gruesome stuff. I usually listen to it while I'm doing the dishes. I finally bought those yellow rubber gloves because the hot water was destroying my cuticles. My sister swears by this almond oil cuticle pen, but I keep losing it in the bottom of my purse. My purse is like a black hole right now, honestly. I found a receipt from 2019 in there the other day. It was for a coffee shop that isn't even open anymore, the one on Elm Street that got turned into a bank. Why do we need so many banks? There are like three on that one block now. It's ridiculous... but wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, thoughts about dying. No, no, I don't have those. I really don't.
Jessica, would you say that you've completely lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, like dance class or game night with your friends?

Um, yeah, actually... that's kind of why I came in. I just barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. Dance class, hiking, trying new recipes, even game night with my friends... they all just sit there now like chores I keep putting off. Which is crazy because I used to love game night. We would play this one board game, Settlers of Catan, have you heard of it? It's all about trading sheep and wheat and stuff. 

My friend Sarah always tries to hoard all the ore, and it drives everyone crazy. Last time we played, she spilled red wine all over the board. It was a brand new bottle, too, a Malbec from Trader Joe's. I love Trader Joe's, but their parking lots are always a nightmare. The one by my house has these tiny spaces, and everyone drives those massive SUVs now. I saw a guy in a giant white truck take up three spots last week. Three! And he just strolled into the store like he owned the place. He was wearing these bright yellow Crocs, which, I mean, I know they're comfortable, but bright yellow? It's a choice. I bought a pair of fuzzy slippers off Amazon last month, and my dog chewed the heel off the left one within ten minutes of me opening the box. He's a terrier mix, so he just destroys everything... but yeah, I just don't have the energy for any of that stuff anymore. I just stay home.
Jessica, would you say that most days, you feel down or low for most of the day, even if it's not extremely intense?

Um, down or low? Not really, no. I mean, I have my moments, but I wouldn't say I feel sad most of the day. It's more just... I don't know, I just feel kind of blank, you know? But speaking of feeling low, did you see the weather forecast for this weekend? It's supposed to rain for three days straight. Which is just great, because my roof has been leaking right above the kitchen sink. 

I called the landlord about it like two weeks ago, and he sent this guy over who just slapped some weird grey putty on the ceiling and called it a day. The putty smells like old cheese, I swear. And it didn't even fix the leak! Now every time it rains, I have to put this orange plastic bucket on the counter. The bucket actually belongs to my neighbor, Mrs. Higgins. She uses it for her gardening. She grows these massive tomatoes, like the size of softballs. She gave me one last summer, and I tried to make a BLT with it, but the bacon I bought was mostly fat. Have you noticed how expensive bacon is getting? It's like eight dollars for a tiny package now. And half the time it's sliced so thin you can see right through it. I saw a TikTok hack where you bake the bacon in the oven instead of frying it, and it's supposed to be crispier, but I always forget to set a timer and end up burning it. The smoke alarm in my apartment is super sensitive, too. If I even look at the stove, it goes off. It's one of those hardwired ones, so you can't just take the battery out, you have to fan it with a towel for like ten minutes... but anyway, no, I don't think I feel depressed or down all day. Just, you know, not really interested in much.
Jessica, have you found that even things that used to bring you small pleasures, like a good cup of coffee, a nice walk, or talking to someone you care about, just don’t feel as good anymore?

Yeah, it's exactly like that. Like I was saying before, I just... I came in because I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. Dance class, hiking, trying new recipes, game night... they all just sit there now like chores I keep putting off. Even the small stuff, like you said, a good cup of coffee. I used to go to this little cafe on 4th Street every Sunday morning. They had these amazing almond croissants. But last time I went, it just tasted like cardboard. 

Actually, the whole cafe has changed since they got a new manager. He painted the walls this awful shade of green, like split pea soup. I hate split pea soup. My grandma used to force me to eat it when I was a kid. She would sit at the table and watch me until I finished every last bite. She had this weird collection of porcelain dolls staring at me from the china cabinet, too. Their eyes were painted so they looked like they were following you around the room. I swear one of them blinked at me once. I tried to tell my mom, but she just said I had an overactive imagination. She's always saying that. Like last week, I told her I thought the mailman was reading my magazines before he delivered them because the pages were all crinkled, and she just rolled her eyes... but yeah, even coffee and stuff. It just doesn't do anything for me anymore.
Jessica, would you say that for most days over the past two years, you’ve felt down or low in your mood for most of the day, even if it wasn’t extremely intense?

Wait, didn't we just talk about this? No, I really wouldn't say I've been feeling down or sad most days, even if we're looking at the last two years. Like I said earlier, it's not a low mood, it's just... I just feel blank. 

But wow, two years... thinking about it, two years ago is exactly when my sister moved down to Florida. She got this apartment in Orlando, right near Disney World. She was so excited because she thought she'd go to the parks all the time, but honestly, it is so incredibly humid down there. Have you ever been to Florida in August? It is literally like walking through a bowl of warm soup. She had to buy this giant dehumidifier for her living room, and it is so loud it sounds like a jet engine taking off. She has to turn the thing completely off just to hear her TV. 

She watches a ton of those true crime documentaries on Netflix. I tried watching one with her over FaceTime a couple of days ago, but my wifi kept cutting out. My internet provider is the absolute worst. I swear they just keep raising my bill by like four or five dollars every few months, hoping I won't notice. I actually tried calling their customer service line on Tuesday, and I was on hold for forty-five minutes listening to this awful elevator music. It was like a smooth jazz version of that Celine Dion song from Titanic. Who even records something like that? It was driving me crazy. I eventually just hung up because my phone battery was dying. My phone never holds a charge anymore... but anyway, yeah, no. I definitely haven't felt depressed or low for two years. Just kind of empty, I guess.
Jessica, would you say that for most days over the past two years, you’ve had a loss of interest or pleasure in most activities you used to enjoy, even if you weren’t feeling sad or down?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that, too? I feel like we're going in circles here. But yeah, like I said before, it's been a long time... definitely over the past two years, yeah. I came in because I barely care about the things that used to make me feel like myself. Dance class, hiking, trying new recipes, even game night... they all just sit there now like chores I keep putting off. 

Speaking of game night, I used to host it every month, and we'd play Settlers of Catan. Have you ever played that? It gets so competitive. My friend Mark always tries to hoard the sheep cards. It's ridiculous. Last time he came over, he spilled a whole glass of red wine on my beige rug. I tried everything to get it out—baking soda, club soda, this expensive stain remover I bought off an infomercial at 2 AM. Do you ever watch those infomercials when you can't sleep? The ones with the guys yelling about how strong their tape is? I actually bought that tape once because I thought I could use it to fix the sole of my favorite boots. They were these brown leather boots I got on sale at Macy's like five years ago. I loved them so much, but the heel just completely detached one day while I was walking to the bus stop. The bus was running late anyway, which always happens on Tuesdays for some reason. I don't know if it's the driver or the traffic, but... yeah, anyway, the tape didn't hold the shoe together at all. It just left this sticky residue everywhere. But yeah, like I said, I just don't have the energy or interest for game night or hiking or anything anymore.

Jessica, would you say that for most of the past two years, you’ve felt this way—like you’ve lost interest or don’t get pleasure from most of the things you used to enjoy, even when you’re not feeling particularly sad?

I mean, yeah, I know we just went over this, but yes. It's been exactly like that for a long time. It started right after the robbery at that festival job I was working at, which was about two years and three months ago. 

That festival was supposed to be so fun, too. It was one of those big outdoor food and music things, and they had these incredible food trucks lined up for miles. There was this one truck that just sold gourmet grilled cheese sandwiches. I mean, who would have thought you could put fig jam and brie on sourdough and it would taste that good? I actually tried to recreate it at home once, back when I still cared about cooking, but the cheese didn't melt right. I think my pan was too hot. My stove is so temperamental. The front left burner gets blazing hot on the lowest setting, but the back right one takes twenty minutes just to boil water. I called my landlord about it, but he's useless. He's this guy named Gary who always wears socks with sandals. Like, thick white athletic socks with those leather strap sandals. It's such a terrible look. He came over to look at the stove, poked it with a screwdriver for two minutes, and told me it was "character." Who calls a broken stove character? 

He did the same thing when the handle fell off my bathroom door. I had to use a butter knife to pry it open for a week until he finally came back with some super glue. Super glue! On a door handle! It fell off again two days later. I ended up just buying a new handle at Home Depot and watching a YouTube video to figure out how to install it myself. Those DIY videos always make it look so easy, but the guy in the video had all these fancy power tools and I just had a basic Phillips head screwdriver that I got in a cheap toolkit from IKEA. Have you ever tried putting together IKEA furniture? It's a nightmare. I bought this bookshelf from them once, the Billy bookcase I think it's called, and it came with like fifty tiny wooden pegs. I lost three of them immediately because my cat knocked them under the sofa. She loves swatting small things. She found a bottle cap yesterday and played with it for an hour. 

But yeah... what were we talking about? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, since the festival robbery. Two years and three months of just... not caring about any of it.

latest_inference.note: The patient has consistently reported a loss of interest and pleasure in previously enjoyed activities for over two years, without significant depressive mood, changes in energy, weight, psychomotor disturbance, or suicidal ideation. This aligns with persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia).

inference_history.note: The patient describes a loss of interest in activities she previously enjoyed, suggesting anhedonia, which is a key symptom of major depressive disorder. The range of candidates reflects varying severity levels of MDD (from mild to unspecified). No disorders have been ruled out yet.

The patient has consistently denied feeling down or depressed most days, which rules out major depressive disorder (F32.0-F32.3) and persistent depressive disorder (F32.8 is adjustment with depressed mood, not chronic). The remaining candidates are F32.8 (depressive disorder not otherwise specified) and F32.9 (unspecified depressive episode), as the patient presents with anhedonia and impaired concentration for over two years without meeting full criteria for a specific depressive disorder.

The patient has described a persistent loss of interest and pleasure in nearly all activities for over two years, without significant depressive symptoms such as low mood, sleep disturbance, appetite changes, or psychomotor slowing. This supports a diagnosis of Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia). The duration and chronic nature of the symptoms differentiate this from Major Depressive Disorder, which tends to have a more acute onset and episodic course. The diagnostic criteria align more closely with F33.x codes, which represent Recurrent Depressive Disorder, as the patient's symptoms have been chronic and ongoing for at least two years.
